paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. Two people come to Jesus in two totally different ways. One is a synagogue leader, a man with a big title, who kneels and says, "My daughter has just died." The other is a woman who has suffered from bleeding for twelve years and comes up behind Him to touch the fringe of His cloak (Matthew 9:18, 20).

Now look at how Jesus treats them. He doesn't brush either one off. He turns, sees the woman, and says, "Take courage, daughter," and He takes the girl by the hand (Matthew 9:22, 25). Big title or no title, a request said out loud or a thought said to herself, He stops for both. I think that's the lesson right there: nobody is too small, too late or too far back in the line for Him.

And then there's that crowd, laughing at Jesus (Matthew 9:24). I'm telling you, friend, I've been laughed at, and it never feels good. But their laughing didn't change what He was going to do. So when your situation looks closed, when everybody around you has already decided how it ends, remember that Jesus can still reach in and take you by the hand.
